newsitem.title: USA: USDA okays haying on CRP land in drought areas.
newsitem.headline: USDA okays haying on CRP land in drought areas.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Thursday said it would allow emergency haying on Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) land in areas suffering from drought and other severe weather conditions as of July 1.
USDA said haying will be allowed until August 31, or until disaster conditions no longer exist, whichever comes first.

To qualify, a county must have lost at least 40 percent of its normal hay and pasture production. Also, it must have experienced a 40 percent or higher loss in normal precipitation or more than 140 percent of normal precipitation, USDA said.
It said only livestock operations located within approved counties are eligible for the emergency haying.
CRP rental payments will be reduced to account for the acres hayed. Other restrictions and limitations also apply, the department said.
Last week, USDA okayed emergency grazing on CRP land in drought areas.
